chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to the servants in the distribution of reward.
And no deed performed by a worshipper is lost with Him, but He will hold them accountable for what they have earned.

key_terms.الظَّالِم: Unjust, one who deprives others of their due
key_terms.عَابِد: Worpper, one who engages in acts of devotion

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about divine justice and the preservation of good deeds?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) affirmation of divine justice (*Adl*), emphasizing that Allah’s accounting is precise and never unjust regarding the distribution of rewards. This narration underscores the Shia theological principle that every good deed is preserved and rewarded, while accountability is strictly proportional to individual actions, reflecting the balance between divine mercy and justice.
